user_steering: Return to task-driven joint gate/expert training; gate-mediated expert differentiation is the central research question.
primary_question: Does QuantumGate induce a more useful and efficient co-evolution of routing and expert function under matched task training?

interpretation.coupling: Gate changes expert exposure and gradient weighting; developing expert functions change task feedback to the gate. Treat specialization as a coupled process.
interpretation.prior_frozen_study: Completed mechanism diagnosis and architecture calibration. Teacher retention is not the primary selection rule for the next stage.
interpretation.existing_joint_training: Earlier autoregressive and routing-stability experiments already trained full models jointly. Next work would evaluate the newly diagnosed reencoding structures and the formation of specialization.

proposed_first_comparison.initialization: Train from scratch; share non-router initial weights and data streams across methods within each seed. Experts remain distinct within a model.
proposed_first_comparison.replication: At least three independent training seeds for a formal comparison; smoke tests precede formal allocation.
proposed_first_comparison.objective: Task next-token cross-entropy with a common expert-load rule. No imitation teacher objective in the primary comparison.
proposed_first_comparison.scope: Jointly train gate, experts and backbone in every routed module of the same causal LM.
fairness: Same expert count, top-k and backbone
Actual router parameters and active computation recorded
Initial load/entropy and gradient health checked
Equal-token and equal-time comparisons reported separately
proposed_first_comparison.selection: Predeclared train-only internal development policy; previously observed validation is exploratory; choose independent held-out evaluation before final selection.

mechanism_measurements: Measure early, middle and late checkpoints on fixed token windows: routing exposure, expert update magnitude, usage and functional differences.
Separate descriptive activation specialization from causal usefulness using controlled expert replacement or suppression and resulting task-loss changes.
Track how one input update changes preferences for several experts, testing architecture-induced coupling against functional complementarity.
Do not assume expert identities align across runs or that each expert represents one semantic task; compare functional behavior and controlled interventions.

geometry_role.first_step: Use functional geometry and sparse tangent directions as diagnostics during joint training; do not immediately add all prior auxiliary losses.
geometry_role.moving_target: Expert outputs and their geometry evolve. Any later geometry-based objective must use current or lagged online estimates, not the old frozen teacher Gram.
geometry_role.collapse_risk: A direct penalty making expert outputs similar can erase specialization. Evaluate any delayed weak router-only or detached-statistic intervention separately, with matched classical controls.
geometry_role.next_decision: Add a low-cost intervention only after observing a reproducible joint-training failure or useful geometry-task association.

literature_checked.finding: For the studied linear-router/SwiGLU MoE, router and expert input-side gradients accumulate shared routed-token directions. Architecture-specific derivation; extension to nonlinear QuantumGate and MoTE tensor experts requires a separate check.
Sections7.1-7.3 report specialization dependent on model component and training setup, including multilingual experts that do not divide by language.
